note: All tasks and model openings are original.

tasks.title: A story opening: The Locked Door
tasks.prompt: Write the opening of a story in which a character finds a door that has always been locked — but today it is open.
plan: Who is your character and where are they?
What do they see, hear and feel as they notice the door?
What tiny detail makes the reader want to read on?
End on a moment of suspense.
criteria: I described the setting using at least two senses
I showed my character’s feelings through actions, not just “she was scared”
I used at least one simile or metaphor
I varied my sentence openings (e.g. a fronted adverbial)
I used a short sentence for effect
I punctuated any speech correctly
I ended with suspense
tasks.model: The corridor smelled of dust and old paper, the way it always did. Mina had walked past the door at the end a thousand times. It was painted the colour of storm clouds and it had never — not once — been open. Today, a thin line of golden light was spilling across the floorboards.

tasks.title: Letter to the head teacher: A school garden
tasks.prompt: Write a letter to your head teacher persuading them to create a school garden.
plan: Opening: who you are and what you are asking for
Reason 1 with evidence or an example
Reason 2 with evidence or an example
Polite closing with a clear request
criteria: I used a formal greeting and sign-off
I stated my request clearly in the first paragraph
I gave at least two reasons, each in its own paragraph
I used persuasive techniques (rhetorical question, facts, emotive language)
I answered a possible objection
I used linking words (furthermore, however, therefore)
I kept a polite, formal tone throughout
tasks.model:
Dear Mrs Okafor,
I am writing on behalf of Class 6B to ask you to consider creating a garden in the empty space behind the hall. We believe it would benefit every pupil in the school.

tasks.title: Report: An amazing animal
tasks.prompt: Write a non-chronological report about an animal of your choice for a children’s encyclopedia.
criteria: I wrote an introduction that tells the reader what the report is about
I organised information into paragraphs with clear topics
I used subheadings
I used present tense and an impersonal style
I included technical vocabulary
I included at least one fact using numbers
I ended with an interesting conclusion
tasks.model: The axolotl is a type of salamander found only in the lakes and canals near Mexico City. Unlike most amphibians, it spends its whole life underwater.

tasks.title: Diary: The day everything went wrong
tasks.prompt: Write a diary entry about a day when everything seemed to go wrong — but ended well.
plan: Set the scene: date and how the day began
Two or three things that went wrong, in order
How you felt at each stage
criteria: I wrote in the first person
I used the past tense for events
I used time connectives to show order
I showed my feelings and thoughts
I used an informal, personal tone
I included a reflection at the end
I checked my spelling and punctuation
tasks.model:
Tuesday 4th March
Dear Diary,
If I had known what today had in store, I would have stayed under my duvet. It started with the alarm clock that never rang…

tasks.title: Instructions: How to make a bee hotel
tasks.prompt: Write clear instructions for a younger pupil explaining how to make a simple bee hotel.
plan: A final tip or safety note
criteria: I included a clear title and goal
I listed the equipment needed
I used numbered steps in the correct order
I started steps with imperative verbs (Cut, Place, Fix)
I used precise vocabulary and measurements
I added a helpful tip or safety warning
My instructions are short and easy to follow
tasks.model:
How to Make a Bee Hotel
Give solitary bees a safe place to nest!
You will need: an empty tin can, 20 paper straws, string, scissors.
1. Wash the tin carefully and remove any sharp edges.

tasks.title: Description: A market at dawn
tasks.prompt: Describe a busy market as it opens early in the morning.
plan: First impression: what you notice first
criteria: I used all five senses across the piece
I used precise nouns and powerful verbs
I used at least two figurative techniques
I varied sentence length
I organised the description in a clear order (e.g. near to far)
I avoided repeating words
I ended with a memorable image
tasks.model: Before the sun had cleared the rooftops, the market was already stirring. Crates thudded onto trestle tables, and the sharp scent of oranges cut through the cool air.
